tells: 1. The laugh doesn't build: across 1.0 s only two people change at all (the white-blouse woman lifts a hand to her chest, the green-hoodie man dips his head), while the purple-top and grey-jacket women at the right table hold the same hands-on-table pose in every frame. No shoulder shake, no breath, no head tip back, no contagion spreading from one person to the next (club-5-strip.png, all six frames, right table and centre table)

2. Repeated identical rest pose: almost everyone sits upright with both forearms flat on the table edge and hands in the same mirrored claw, like mannequins posed at a desk, with no leaning on an elbow, drinks in hand, crossed arms or turning to a friend (club-1-wide.png, front row across the full width; club-6-held.png, centre table)

3. The face close is a game cutscene face: plastic skin with a uniform orange cast and no pores or specular breakup, glassy painted eyes with no wet line or moist lid rim, a stiff half-open mouth with no cheek raise (no Duchenne in the 'laugh'), and a dark cutout halo where the DOF meets the shoulder (club-4-face.png, face centre and the shoulder/background edge on the right)

4. Back rows are flat black cardboard cutouts standing in a grid, and the same silhouettes repeat; none of them moves between frames, so the room is visibly only the front ~12 people (club-1-wide.png, centre band behind the front tables; club-5-strip.png, upper left)

5. Hair is helmet-like mesh with hard edges and no flyaways or translucency against the backlight; the blonde buns and bobs read as plastic (club-2-mid.png, blonde woman far right table and the bun behind the green hoodie; club-6-held.png, man in the cap)

1. Bodies don't sit in the seats: people float above the red seat cushions with thighs horizontal in midair and no compression or seat-back contact, and the second row's torsos rise straight out of the seat backs like cardboard standees (theatre-1-wide.png, front two rows; theatre-6-held.png, second row behind the front row)

2. Identical hands-clasped-on-knees pose repeated across the whole front row, symmetrical and parade-ground upright; no one slouches, crosses legs, leans on an armrest or toward a neighbour (theatre-1-wide.png, front row; theatre-3-mid.png, front row)

3. The laugh is two or three people opening their mouths: the light-blue-top woman and the green-hoodie man go open-mouthed by t=12.8 but their shoulders, chests and heads barely move, and everyone else is frozen; the onset reads as a mouth swap, not a laugh building through the body (theatre-5-strip.png, t=12.6 to 13.0, front row centre)

4. The back stands are a grid of identically lit, evenly spaced figures standing bolt upright with arms down, an obvious wallpaper/impostor crowd with no motion at all (theatre-1-wide.png, top half; theatre-2-mid.png, upper band)

5. The face close has a dead, uncanny laugh: dark empty mouth cavity with no tongue or upper teeth shading, eyebrows and eyes that don't engage, flat waxy skin, rubbery hair-cap, and the jacket collar clips into the neck (theatre-4-face.png, mouth and eyes centre, collar lower right)

1. The laugh onset is the best of the three but still a cut-and-paste: the green-top and black-hoodie women turn to each other and open their mouths in near-sync by t=12.8, while the four men to the left keep the same pose and only rotate their heads a few degrees; no body pump, no hand coming up, no one leaning back (openmic-5-strip.png, t=12.6 to 13.0, centre and left)

2. Everyone sits with hands planted on knees in the same pose and the same elbow angle, a row of mannequins; front row figures are also pressed shoulder to shoulder at an impossible density with bodies interpenetrating (openmic-1-wide.png, front row; openmic-3-mid.png, yellow shirt into the green top)

3. Chairs are barely visible and bodies hover; feet and lower legs dissolve into black with no floor contact or shadow, so the crowd floats in a void (openmic-1-wide.png, bottom third; openmic-6-held.png, bottom edge)

4. The face close is a game NPC: plastic skin with no pores, eyes painted with no wet line, a hairline that is a hard texture edge, dark DOF halo around the head and the blurred woman behind, and a necklace that sits pasted on the skin (openmic-4-face.png, face centre, hairline top, background edge right)

5. The back of the room is a few flat silhouettes and an empty dark wall with a floating green dot; the room is too clean and too sparse for an open mic, with no bar clutter, phones or movement (openmic-1-wide.png, centre back and left door)
